coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Pipeline LLMCodeChoice: (1) amostra N programas do LLM para uma descricao de tarefa; (2) teste diferencial (fuzzing com Hypothesis e execucao simbolica com CrossHair) encontra inputs distinguidores que separam os programas em clusters de comportamento equivalente; (3) inferencia de oraculo via LLM: um prompt de multipla escolha com chain-of-thought pede ao LLM para escolher a saida correta para cada input distinguidor, eliminando iterativamente os clusters incorretos ate restar um; (4) o cluster restante e retornado ao usuario junto com a especificacao input-output inferida.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo apoia a identificacao/geracao de Relacoes Metamorficas (MRs), que sao usadas como oraculo de teste em Metamorphic Testing (MT) para atenuar o problema do oraculo. Nao gera casos de teste nem inputs; avalia se o LLM consegue propor MRs validas e corretas para 37 programas sob teste (SUTs) em C, C++, Java e Python.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Framework de duas partes: (1) Geracao de MR - um prompt com Introducao de Conceito + Especificacao do SUT + MRs Codificadas Iniciais (exemplos few-shot) e enviado ao LLM (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 ou gpt-4-1106-preview), que retorna candidatos a MR (MRCs) extraidos dos blocos de codigo da resposta, repetindo a interacao para gerar mais MRCs; (2) Validacao de MR - 'Dual Validation' combinando Teste Aleatorio (1000 inputs executados, repetido 5 vezes, para checar legalidade/corretude automaticamente) e Checagem Manual (dois pos-graduandos validam se a MRC tem subrelacao de entrada e saida e se a implementacao bate com a descricao) antes de aceitar a MRC na lista final de MRs geradas.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo apoia a geracao automatica de testes unitarios (casos de teste com assercoes/oraculo) para programas Python, usando mutation testing como guia para aumentar a eficacia dos testes em revelar bugs (nao so cobertura). Foca em melhorar o oraculo (as assercoes) gerado pelo LLM, nao em gerar inputs ou requisitos.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Pipeline MuTAP: (1) Prompt Inicial (zero-shot ou few-shot) gera um Teste Unitario Inicial (IUT) via LLM; (2) Refinamento - Syntax Fixer (reprompt do LLM para corrigir erros de sintaxe, ou remocao das linhas com erro via parser Python) e Intended Behavior Repair (executa o PUT e corrige assercoes com valor de retorno esperado errado); (3) Mutation Testing via MutPy calcula o Mutation Score (MS) e identifica mutantes sobreviventes; (4) Aumento de Prompt - reprompta o LLM incluindo o IUT, uma instrucao explicando a falha e um mutante sobrevivente especifico, gerando um Augmented Unit Test (AUT), repetindo ate MS=100% ou esgotar os mutantes; (5) Minimizacao de Oraculo - algoritmo guloso remove assercoes redundantes do teste final sem piorar o MS.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Pipeline MATI: (1) Mineracao Intra-App - exploracao inicial de GUI baseada em grafo de transicao de UI (UTG), com OCR e deteccao de texto verticalmente alinhado/titulo para montar um repositorio de dados candidatos (par Label/Data por pagina), mais extracao de rotulo de pagina; (2) Geracao de Input - ao detectar um campo de input tipo 'query' (via condicoes de dica/icone/posicao), filtra dados candidatos das paginas relacionadas no UTG, extrai a 'dica' textual proxima ao campo (deteccao YOLOv5 + OCR + grau de inclusao, refinado por um prompt ao ChatGPT), e envia a dica + dados candidatos ao ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-turbo) com um prompt fixo para recomendar a palavra mais adequada como valor de input. O MATI funciona como um 'hook' plugavel em qualquer ferramenta de teste de GUI black-box existente que forneca screenshots (no estudo, integrado a ferramenta Cvrip).

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Abordagem TAPE (Technology Adoption Performance Evaluation): um modelo generico -> modelo pratico -> modelo instanciado por cenario, que define 'value units', atributos e casos, com uma suite de benchmark percentual (formulas AddedValue e CostOfValueUnit) para comparar releases/estados de adocao de tecnologia. Aplicada ao Tanius, o servico de geracao de teste da area de TI da Volkswagen (parte da plataforma 'Testing as a Service' junto com o T-Rex), que integra tres 'engines' de geracao de teste modulares e independentes: determinista (OpenAPI Generator), evolutiva/busca (EvoMaster) e baseada em LLM (StarCoder/StarCoderChat). Os testes de cada engine sao comparados contra uma suite de referencia escrita manualmente por engenheiros da Volkswagen para duas APIs REST reais (auth-service e user-service).

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The paper targets automatic unit test case generation at the class level for Java, comparing three approaches: search-based software testing (SBST, via EvoSuite), symbolic execution (via Kex), and LLM-based generation (via TestSpark). It also evaluates the resulting test suites' fault-detection/failure-reproduction capability by running them against buggy and patched versions of real GitBug Java projects.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The authors built an open-source 'test generation assessment pipeline' with four stages: benchmarks (project-under-test descriptions from the GitBug Java dataset), a runner that invokes each tool with a 120-second time budget, tool-specific adapters (EvoSuite, Kex, TestSpark), and an analysis module that computes compilation rate, coverage and mutation score and runs statistical tests. For the LLM path specifically, TestSpark follows a three-step flow (prompt collection from the class under test, LLM request, and a feedback loop that iteratively shrinks the prompt and retries on compile errors), using a default prompt that asks for JUnit 4 tests with 100% line coverage, no mocking except via Mockito, and a fixed naming template.

coluna (RQ): RQ3.3 – What are the benefits of fine-tuning or applying prompt engineering for test case genera-
texto original da célula: The paper does not fine-tune any model; only prompt/context engineering (structured prompt plus an automatic feedback loop that shrinks context and retries on failures) is used, and no separate ablation isolates that mechanism's contribution versus a plain single-shot prompt. The clearest 'engineering' effect reported is indirect: performance differences across LLMs are attributed mainly to context-window size rather than to any prompting technique.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The paper targets test oracle generation, specifically producing an ordered sequence of one or more assert statements for a JUnit test method given its focal (production) method, going beyond prior work that generated only a single assertion per test. A second, downstream activity is using the generated assertion sequences to expose real-world bugs on the Defects4J benchmark.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: ALLMASSERT is a two-stage pipeline: (1) an IFT-LLM, obtained by parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA) of codellama-34B-instruct on Methods2Test (focal method + test method with placeholders -> assert sequence) pairs, directly generates an initial assertion sequence; (2) a RAG- and chain-of-thought-driven refinement stage feeds that draft, plus static-analysis-retrieved project context (method call traceback, constant/variable checks, assertion-count checks, type checks), back into the original (non-fine-tuned) codellama-34B-instruct to correct hallucinated or incomplete assertions before they are inserted into the test method.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The paper addresses crowdsourced test-report triage: given a large set of textual bug reports submitted by crowdworkers, the LLM is used to cluster reports by the type of bug they reveal, and a subsequent algorithm turns that clustering into a prioritized inspection sequence for app developers. This is a report-analysis/prioritization activity rather than code or test-case generation.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: LLMPrior has two stages: (1) Report Clustering, where a single structured zero-shot chain-of-thought prompt (basic info + fine-grained clustering instructions with worked examples + a required hierarchical-tree output format + an explicit step-by-step instruction) feeds all reports' textual descriptions to GPT-4-Turbo, which returns a hierarchical cluster tree (root = all reports, internal nodes = sub-clusters, leaves = individual reports); (2) Report Prioritization, a deterministic recurrent-selection algorithm (GenerateSequence/UpdateStatus/SelectReport) that walks the tree, repeatedly picking the least-visited report from the least-visited branch, to output a deduplicated prioritized report sequence that evenly distributes reports of the same bug type.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The paper evaluates LLMs on three testing activities: system-level test case generation (write test cases for a given application/URL covering specific functions), error tracing (given a real error message, explain the likely root cause), and bug localization (given a code snippet, identify the likely location of the bug). A 'follow-up question' method (re-asking the LLM if it missed any bugs) is also tested as a refinement step.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo foca em geração/aprimoramento de testes unitários (unit test generation), especificamente na etapa de pós-processamento de testes já gerados por uma ferramenta de teste baseada em busca (SBST), visando aumentar a compreensibilidade (understandability) desses testes automatizados para apoiar a atividade de correção de bugs (bug-fixing) por desenvolvedores.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: UTGen combina EvoSuite (SBST) com um LLM em quatro estágios encadeados: 1) refinamento de dados de teste (o LLM substitui valores aleatórios por dados contextualizados), 2) pós-processamento (o LLM adiciona comentários no formato Given-When-Then e melhora nomes de variáveis), 3) sugestão de nome do método de teste com base no corpo já enriquecido, e 4) compilação/verificação, com um parser e heurísticas (checagem via CodeBLEU, até 3 re-prompts) para lidar com alucinações do LLM antes de aceitar o teste final.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Reparo automático (repair) de testes flaky do tipo non-idempotent-outcome (NIO) — testes que passam na primeira execução mas falham em reexecuções subsequentes no mesmo ambiente devido à poluição de estado compartilhado; o estudo também cobre a detecção desses testes via análise dinâmica e a extração de contexto/código relevante para orientar o reparo.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: NIODebugger é um framework de três fases com um agente baseado em LLM: 1) Detecção — reexecuta os testes em ambiente isolado (class loader isolado) coletando resultados e stack traces para identificar possíveis testes NIO; 2) Exploração — o agente LLM decide, via prompts com formato de resposta restrito, qual código-fonte adicional precisa (método, classe, arquivo similar ou inferência de nome de método) entre cinco workflows parametrizados; 3) Correção — o LLM gera o patch usando o código coletado, stack traces de múltiplas reexecuções e um exemplo one-shot, com uma fase opcional de reflexão (até 3 iterações) caso o patch falhe.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Geração de oráculos de teste (test oracle generation) — especificamente oráculos de asserção (assertion oracles) e de exceção (exception oracles) para casos de teste JUnit, dado um prefixo de teste e o método sob teste (MUT), usados posteriormente para detecção de mutantes e de bugs reais.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Geração de testes de segurança voltados a confirmar a explorabilidade de vulnerabilidades: geração de casos de teste unitários (JUnit) que disparam (trigger) vulnerabilidades conhecidas de bibliotecas de terceiros (TPLs) quando alcançáveis a partir da interface de acesso do usuário em um projeto cliente Java.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: VULEUT tem três fases: 1) Preparação de dados — extrai a estrutura do projeto cliente e informações do PoC da vulnerabilidade, localiza métodos vulneráveis e constrói grafos/caminhos de chamada de método (via Soot, algoritmo Spark); 2) Análise de caminho alcançável — constrói um Parameter Transfer Graph (PTG) por caminho de chamada e aplica quatro regras de propagação (Propagação Direta, Conversão de Tipo, Mudança de Valor, Não Propagação) para filtrar caminhos onde o parâmetro que dispara a vulnerabilidade realmente se propaga da entrada do usuário até o código vulnerável; 3) Geração de teste de exploração — extrai input/oráculo/método focal/contexto e usa um prompt few-shot para o ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-turbo) gerar testes JUnit que usam um MethodCallInterceptor (via ByteBuddy) para checar tanto que a chamada vulnerável foi disparada (isTriggered) quanto que a condição da vulnerabilidade foi satisfeita (isConditionMet), compilando e executando os testes para confirmar a exploração.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo aborda geracao de testes de aceitacao (acceptance testing) para aplicacoes web em dois passos: (i) geracao de cenarios de teste de aceitacao em linguagem natural (Gherkin) a partir de user stories, apoiando ATDD/BDD; e (ii) geracao de scripts de teste executaveis (Cypress/TypeScript) a partir desses cenarios Gherkin e do HTML das paginas sob teste.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Duas ferramentas encadeadas foram implementadas: AutoUAT recebe titulo e descricao da user story e gera cenarios de aceitacao em Gherkin via prompt iterativamente refinado; Test Flow recebe a user story, os cenarios Gherkin e o HTML das paginas (limpo de estilo/script) e gera o script Cypress correspondente, com integracao a JIRA e a um GitHub Action que roda os testes automaticamente em pull requests.

coluna (RQ): RQ3.2 – How do LLM-generated test cases compare with manually created or traditional automated test generation approaches?
texto original da célula: O proprio estudo nao inclui um experimento direto comparando Test Flow/AutoUAT contra uma abordagem manual ou uma ferramenta automatizada tradicional; a comparacao com baselines nao-LLM (ex.: geracao manual, Selenium, Capture&Replay) aparece apenas de forma qualitativa na secao de trabalhos relacionados, citando estudos de terceiros.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo e uma avaliacao critica de ferramentas de geracao de testes unitarios baseadas em LLM ja em uso comercial/pratico (GitHub Copilot e Qodo Cover), focada especificamente em como elas lidam com codigo humano defeituoso (buggy) e se os testes gerados conseguem detectar ou, ao contrario, validar bugs (problema do oraculo de teste).

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Nao ha um framework novo proposto; os autores montam um pipeline de avaliacao: cada implementacao defeituosa (OG) do dataset Refactory, junto com sua solucao de referencia (REF), e usada para gerar uma suite de testes com cada ferramenta; cada teste gerado e executado contra OG e REF e classificado em 4 categorias (falha em OG/passa em REF; falha em ambos; passa em ambos; passa em OG e falha em REF), permitindo distinguir testes que detectam bugs de testes que os validam.

coluna (RQ): RQ2.2 – Which approaches (e.g., fine-tuning, ICL, prompt engineering) have LLMs been applied for test case generation?
texto original da célula: O estudo nao propoe nem aplica fine-tuning ou engenharia de prompt propria; e uma analise empirica do comportamento de ferramentas ja existentes usadas com parametros padrao (Copilot via comando 'Generate Tests'; Qodo Cover ate 100% de cobertura ou 5 tentativas).

coluna (RQ): RQ3.3 – What are the benefits of fine-tuning or applying prompt engineering for test case genera-
texto original da célula: Nao se aplica: o artigo nao testa nem propoe uma tecnica propria de fine-tuning ou prompt engineering; apenas usa as ferramentas comerciais como caixa-preta com configuracoes padrao.

coluna (RQ): RQ4.3 – What are the costs (time, computational resources, prompt engineering) of generating test cases with LLMs compared to traditional approaches?
texto original da célula: O artigo nao reporta custo monetario nem tempo de execucao proprios das ferramentas avaliadas; menciona apenas, citando outro trabalho (Meta TestGen-LLM), que cerca de 30% dos testes gerados sao rejeitados durante revisao humana, sem quantificar esse custo em tempo ou dinheiro.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo trata de geracao de casos de teste a partir de requisitos escritos em linguagem natural (ingles), comparando a capacidade de seis LLMs de uso geral em produzir testes que sejam usados depois em um modelo Simulink correspondente ao requisito.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Processo de 5 etapas: (1) criacao de 25 requisitos em linguagem natural com complexidades variadas (complexidade ciclomatica de 3 a 41); (2) criacao manual de um modelo Simulink para cada requisito; (3) geracao de casos de teste pelos 6 LLMs a partir de um unico prompt fixo aplicado a cada requisito; (4) geracao de casos de teste de referencia pelo SLDV (Simulink Design Verifier) a partir do proprio modelo; (5) execucao dos casos de teste no modelo e extracao de metricas de cobertura (decisao, condicao, MCDC, execucao).

coluna (RQ): RQ3.3 – What are the benefits of fine-tuning or applying prompt engineering for test case genera-
texto original da célula: Nao ha isolamento do beneficio de engenharia de prompt ou fine-tuning: o mesmo prompt generico foi usado para todos os LLMs e requisitos, especificamente para manter a comparacao imparcial; os autores afirmam explicitamente que testar prompts diferentes esta fora do escopo deste estudo e sera tratado em trabalho futuro.

coluna (RQ): RQ4.3 – What are the costs (time, computational resources, prompt engineering) of generating test cases with LLMs compared to traditional approaches?
texto original da célula: Nao reportado: o artigo exclui explicitamente do escopo aspectos de eficiencia e tempo de geracao dos casos de teste ('aspects related to the efficiency of test case generation, including the time taken to produce these test cases, have also been excluded from consideration'), nao havendo nenhum numero de custo monetario ou de tempo.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo trata de geracao automatica de testes unitarios para linguagens dinamicamente tipadas (Python), cobrindo tres atividades encadeadas: inferencia/anotacao de tipos de parametros ausentes, geracao evolutiva de casos de teste guiada por LLM, e reparo automatico de erros de sintaxe/execucao nas suites geradas.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Framework pytLMtester com 3 modulos: (1) pre-processamento, onde o LLM analisa o codigo e a docstring para anotar tipos de parametros nao tipados (com fatiamento do prompt quando excede o limite de tokens); (2) DynaMOSA-LLMmutate, que estende o algoritmo evolutivo DynaMOSA do Pynguin, chamando o LLM 5 vezes a cada 50 iteracoes via cadeia de pensamento (primeiro identifica dificuldades, depois gera dados de teste) para mutar individuos de alta qualidade; (3) pos-processamento, que detecta erros de sintaxe (analise de parse tree) e de execucao e os envia iterativamente (ate 5 tentativas) ao LLM para reparo.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: O estudo trata de geracao automatica de casos de teste unitarios (input+oraculo) para programas em C diretamente a partir de enunciados de problema em linguagem natural, opcionalmente acompanhados da solucao de referencia e de exemplos de teste, avaliando corretude funcional (Pass@1) e cobertura de linhas.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Pipeline experimental: um system prompt fixo define o formato de saida e a tarefa; um user prompt e montado a partir de um banco de 40 problemas C originais (variando enunciado apenas, solucao em C, solucao em Python, ou solucao em C + 3 exemplos de teste); cada um dos 5 LLMs gera exatamente 10 casos de teste (input/output) em arquivos padronizados; os casos gerados sao validados executando a solucao de referencia em C e comparando a saida, e entao sao computadas as metricas Pass@1 e cobertura de linha (via LCOV/gcov).

coluna (RQ): RQ4.3 – What are the costs (time, computational resources, prompt engineering) of generating test cases with LLMs compared to traditional approaches?
texto original da célula: Nao reportado: o artigo nao apresenta nenhum valor de custo monetario (API) nem tempo de execucao proprio dos experimentos realizados.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: Geração de testes unitários (unit test generation) em tempo real, integrada a um plugin de IDE, com suporte multi-linguagem (Java, Python e Golang) usando o mesmo pipeline; inclui também a detecção e correção automática de erros de compilação/hallucinations nos testes gerados, sem exigir compilação do projeto inteiro.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: LspAi opera em duas etapas principais orquestradas via Language Server Protocol (LSP): (1) Análise de Dependência — filtragem de tokens relevantes do método focal, recuperação de definições (Definition Provider) e de referências de uso (Reference Provider) para montar um contexto de dependência enxuto; (2) Geração de Teste Unitário — constrói um prompt (baseado no template do ChatUniTest, adaptado para outras linguagens) com o código do método focal, descrição em linguagem natural e as dependências recuperadas, envia ao LLM para gerar o teste, verifica o resultado via LSP Diagnosis Provider (sem compilar/executar) e, se houver erro, recupera dependências adicionais relacionadas ao erro e reenvia ao LLM para corrigir (Dependency-Aware Error Fix), repetindo até resolver ou atingir o limite de iterações.

The prompt-engineering benefit is not isolated via a controlled ablation against a naive/unstructured prompt; the paper instead notes, as a limitation/future-work point, that achieving a high compilation rate 'is unlikely to be fully achieved with prompt engineering alone,' leaving optimization of the prompting scheme (e.g., via backtracking/code-analysis frameworks like ROCODE) for future work rather than demonstrating a measured PE-specific gain.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: No fine-tuning is performed; ASTER relies entirely on prompting six off-the-shelf LLMs (GPT-4-turbo, Llama3-70B/8B, CodeLlama-34B, Granite-34B/8B) guided by static analysis, so no fine-tuning gain is reported. coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: No fine-tuning is used; SAGEN combines static analysis (for value-range identification of numeric/boolean/enum/index literals) with a single GPT-4 prompting step (only for string literals) to derive input ranges, then randomly samples values within those ranges. The paper does not isolate a gain attributable specifically to the LLM step versus static analysis alone, since the two are used for disjoint literal types (LLM for strings, static analysis/heuristics for everything else).

coluna (RQ): RQ3.3 – What are the benefits of fine-tuning or applying prompt engineering for test case genera-
texto original da célula: No fine-tuning is used, so any benefit is attributed to the narrow prompt-engineering step for string-literal regex generation combined with static analysis; the paper does not run an ablation isolating the LLM-regex step's specific contribution to overall coverage/compilation, since the LLM is only one of several range-identification mechanisms (used solely for strings) working alongside purely static heuristics for other literal types.

coluna (RQ): RQ4.3 – What are the costs (time, computational resources, prompt engineering) of generating test cases with LLMs compared to traditional approaches?
texto original da célula: The paper reports no dollar, token, or wall-clock time cost for either the static-analysis steps or the GPT-4 regex-generation calls; only the hardware used for experiments (Intel i7-9700K, 16GB RAM, Ubuntu 20.04) is mentioned, with no runtime or API expenditure figures given.

coluna (RQ): RQ4.3 – What are the costs (time, computational resources, prompt engineering) of generating test cases with LLMs compared to traditional approaches?
texto original da célula: No dollar/API cost is reported for querying the three LLMs via the Poe platform. The paper does report compute specs used for running the pre-LLM DeepSTL baseline tool in Experiment 2 (a machine with 80 CPU cores, 251GB RAM, 12GB GPU VRAM, 870GB disk, openEuler 20.03 LTS), but this reflects the cost of the non-LLM comparison method, not of the LLMs themselves.

coluna (RQ): RQ3.2 – How do LLM-generated test cases compare with manually created or traditional automated test generation approaches?
texto original da célula: The paper poses a research question (RQ3) about comparing LLM-generated tests to 'traditional test generation methods,' but the results section only reports comparisons among the four LLMs themselves via JEST/Stryker metrics -- no non-LLM automated tool (e.g., EvoSuite/TestSpark) or manually written test baseline is actually run or reported, so this comparison is not empirically answered despite being announced in the introduction.

coluna (RQ): RQ3.3 – What are the benefits of fine-tuning or applying prompt engineering for test case genera-

coluna (RQ): RQ4.3 – What are the costs (time, computational resources, prompt engineering) of generating test cases with LLMs compared to traditional approaches?

coluna (RQ): RQ2.1 – Which LLM models are most used/effective to automate test cases?
texto original da célula: The paper does not name or evaluate any specific LLM (no GPT/Claude/Llama model identifier appears in the text); it describes the LLM Interaction Layer generically as able to integrate with 'different models' via prompt templates and multi-turn conversation management, so no comparative claim about which model is more effective is made.

This is an explicitly labeled 'short paper' describing only the conceptual framework, illustrated with one worked example (Table I, a single live mutant in a withdraw() function) showing the hypothesis-refinement loop succeeding after one failed iteration; no coverage, mutation-score, or accuracy figures across a benchmark are given.

coluna (RQ): RQ3.2 – How do LLM-generated test cases compare with manually created or traditional automated test generation approaches?

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: LISP targets automated input generation / test-input-space partitioning for Java library API testing, aimed at maximizing edge/branch coverage and triggering exceptions (i.e., finding defects and previously-unknown vulnerabilities) in library APIs; it focuses purely on input generation and test-suite assembly, not on oracle/assertion synthesis beyond exception-triggering, nor on requirement extraction, repair or prioritization.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: LISP's framework: (1) an LLM is given the signature and source code of the library API under test and prompted to infer and partition the method's input space, producing a natural-language description of each partition (e.g., conditions on parameter sign/nullity/type); (2) the LLM is then prompted to sample concrete input values consistent with each partition's textual description; (3) these sampled inputs are assembled into test suites/drivers that instantiate objects (guided by a top-down type dependency analysis, TDA, for constructing valid nested/complex-type objects) and invoke the API method to systematically exercise its behavior; an LISP-CG (deeper-context) variant additionally supplies information about called/dependent functions in the prompt.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The paper targets improving the readability of already-generated Python unit tests (a post-generation refinement/transformation activity), applied to pytest suites originally produced by the Pynguin search-based unit-test generator; it does not itself generate new tests, extract requirements, synthesize oracles or repair/prioritize tests.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The approach manually applies a fixed, ordered sequence of prompts to GPT-4 via the ChatGPT Code Interpreter plug-in, transforming each Pynguin-generated pytest test case in turn: (1) define named constants for hard-coded values, (2) separate the test into setup/execution/assertion phases, (3) remove unnecessary or redundant assertions, (4) use meaningful test and variable names, (5) reformat the code to the PEP 8 style guide, and (6) add documentation/comments explaining the test's purpose, actions and coverage; each transformed test is then added to a rebuilt test suite file.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.1 – How is In-Context-Learning being used to create test cases?

Six intervention strategies are defined across 3 stages x manner: initializing-population (MOSA+LLM-ir/irdm), iterative-population-update (MOSA+LLM-tr/trdm), and test-coverage-plateau (MOSA+LLM-tl/tldm), each optionally paired with a 'dynamic monitor' that halves/doubles the intervention probability or stagnation threshold based on whether the LLM produced a useful new test case. In all strategies, Code Llama is prompted with the module's source code and the test function's header, and its raw output is rewritten/post-processed into Pynguin's test-case format before being merged into the genetic population, which then continues its normal selection/crossover/mutation/replacement loop (Algorithm 1).

texto original da célula: MR-Adopt is a two-phase LLM pipeline. Phase 1 (Input Pairs Preparation): the LLM performs analogical reasoning over the hard-coded source/follow-up input pair to generate additional example input pairs, which are then refined via data-flow analysis (removing irrelevant/erroneous code) and filtered by checking them against the developer-written output relation. Phase 2 (Input Transformation Generation): using the original pair plus the Phase-1-generated pairs as few-shot examples, the LLM generates candidate transformation functions, which are again refined via data-flow analysis and then assessed by applying each candidate to all prepared source inputs, selecting the most generalizable one as the final result.

texto original da célula: Wasabi runs two complementary workflows. Dynamic testing workflow: (1) a static routine (CodeQL control-flow analysis plus naming-convention heuristics, complemented by GPT-4 for non-loop forms) identifies 'retry-location triplets' (coordinator method, retried method, trigger exception); (2) an AspectJ-based fault-injection module throws the trigger exception at that location (K=1 and K=100 times) while running the existing unit test; (3) the three custom oracles flag anomalies in the resulting log; (4) a test planner schedules {test, retry-location} pairs to avoid redundant runs. Static checking workflow: CodeQL computes an application-wide 'retry ratio' per exception type to flag outlier IF-retry-policy bugs, while a series of engineered GPT-4 yes/no prompts (Figure 2) scan each source file for missing-cap/missing-delay WHEN-retry bugs, including in non-loop retry forms (state machines, queues) that CodeQL's control-flow analysis alone cannot recognize.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: TensorJSFuzz is a three-stage pipeline. (1) Constraint Extraction: an AST parser extracts precise parameter type information (structure/rank/shape/dtype/enum) directly from each operator's function signature, while an LLM (ChatGPT/GPT-4, one-shot prompted with a task description and worked example) extracts dependency constraints (value ranges, inter-parameter relations) from the operator's checking code. (2) Input Generation: a heuristic (non-SMT) algorithm first generates type-consistent random inputs, then iteratively adjusts them to satisfy the LLM-extracted dependency constraints via a custom constraint parser built on a hand-derived BNF grammar. (3) Test Oracle: the generated inputs are run through differential testing across the four backends and AddressSanitizer, flagging wrong-computation, crash, and memory bugs.

coluna (RQ): RQ1.2 – What is the gain of fine-tuning or applying the in-context-learning practice to create test cases?
texto original da célula: The pipeline has four components. GUI Explorer: performs in-depth fuzzing of the target app, recording every GUI transition as a tuple <page-before, event, page-after> (XML layout trees). SemanticAgent: annotates each page/event with explicit semantic information (pruning the XML tree from ~148 to ~70 nodes on average, using OCR for WebView pages, and using GPT-4o with screenshots for ambiguous widgets). Graph Builder: clusters the annotated pages/events in real time into a semantically enriched Clustered UI Transition Graph (CUTG), stored in a Neo4j graph database. GenerationAgent: matches each natural-language test step to a path in the CUTG using embedding-similarity filtering (top-50 candidates) plus an LLM for fine-grained selection, with a dynamic recursive rollback mechanism that re-matches the previous step whenever no candidate satisfies the current one, ultimately producing an executable uiautomator2 script.
